title: docs: TypeScript examples in PUBLISHED package READMEs that do not compile — split the #18751 census into published-README vs internal-document blocks and correct the wrong examples in published READMEs only (#18715 ruling F)
body:
Filed by the director seat (objectstack #12708, summon #24, `session_01Wj1HUjzyeiBQ8atRf1ZhaL`) executing decision batch #156 item 2 — maintainer 「同意」 to **F** on #18715: ⛔ no gate is built; the user-facing half of the census is worked here.

## The reading (PR #18751's census instrument, on `main`; re-run before acting)

1,002 TypeScript fenced blocks in package-root Markdown. Hand-written documents: 54 files / 282 blocks — 195 fail to compile; 76 under the tolerant reading (legal elisions allowed); **58 syntactically valid and wrong** (copy-paste fails). CHANGELOGs (720 blocks) are out of scope: they correctly record deleted APIs.

## Ask

1. **Split** the 76 / 58 by publication: a block is *published* when its document is inside its package's `files[]` (README.md and siblings that ship); everything else (`PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, design notes, internal guides) is *internal*. Record both counts on this card with the instrument's output.
2. **Correct** the published-README examples that are syntactically valid and wrong, one PR per package or one PR overall — the claimant's call — so that every example a platform user's AI can copy compiles against the package it documents. A block that documents a removed API is rewritten or deleted, ⛔ never left as a fossil.
3. ⛔ Internal-document blocks are not worked here. If an internal document is dead, deleting it is the fix, on its own card.
4. ⛔ No gate, no ratchet, no CI wiring (ruling F). `Clause-②: no`; changeset `skip-changeset` (docs only) unless a package ships its README changes in a release note by convention.

## Refs

#18715 (ruling F) · PR #18751 (the census instrument) · #15931 · #18620 / PR #18712

Dedup terms: `published README examples compile`, `fenced TypeScript block typecheck`, `files[] published document split`
